name: account-and-login
purpose: Sign-up, log in, password reset, delete account and the update prompt
summary: Email and code sign-up in four steps; "Got an invite link?" accepts the link or code; the profile loads first time and an invite is claimed once it exists. Password reset by emailed code; delete account in Settings; the update prompt when a build is too old. Build 13 adds Sign in with Apple as an equal option (Google is not built; its switch is off).

name: welcome-cards
purpose: The three one-time cards that explain how Mahi works after first sign-in
summary:
Three cards after your first sign-in, shown once per account per phone:
• Post when a friend tags you. You have 48 hours to answer with a photo, front and back camera. Each answer earns you a Mahi point.
• Every post tags 3 friends. They have 48 hours to answer with a workout of their own.
• Post to open your feed. Posting your answer opens your feed for 24 hours. If a friend tags you, it locks until you answer.
The button says Next, then "Start training". There's no skip.

name: camera-and-posting
purpose: When you can post, the two-photo camera, preview, caption and location
summary: You post your first Mahi free (it earns your first point), then only when a mate tags you. The camera says exactly what to do next: "You were tagged by @sam. You have 47:59:59 to post your Mahi and get your first point", or "Post your first Mahi to get your first point and tag 3 mates". Two photos: what you see, then a selfie. Preview, caption (emoji keyboard button from build 13), location, the three mate circles, then post. Waiting for a tag: a card explaining why, with Invite a mate, See your invites and Find mates in your contacts; from the next update you can pull the camera down a little to reveal it. Build 13: Share to Mahi from Photos, Apple's shutter sound, a Control Centre button.

name: tagging
purpose: Every post tags three friends: who can be tagged, who can't, and the nudges
summary: Every post tags 3 mates: friends on Mahi, people on Mahi you don't follow yet (in-app invite), or anyone by link. Three circles fill as you pick them, and the title says "@sam, @ali and @kim will keep you going". A first post that answers a mate's tag needs no tags. You can tag back the mate whose tag you answer; your own open tag on someone blocks tagging them again until they answer. The camera shows your mates on the clock and how long they have.

name: tags-and-48-hours
purpose: The 48-hour window, reminders, missed tags and cancelled tags
summary: Every tag gives 48 hours to post any workout back. The camera counts down to the second: "@sam is waiting on you · 41:20:00 left", yellow under 6 hours with "Only 05:59:59 left to answer @sam". Answering can tag that mate back, so two mates keep each other going. Miss the 48 hours and your points go back to 0 (best stays), shown once as "You missed @sam's tag" the next time you open Mahi; the mate who tagged you is told too. A miss at 0 points sends no points-lost message.

name: mahi-points
purpose: How Mahi points work, and where they show
summary: Your first post earns 1 point. Each answer to a mate's tag earns 1 more. Miss one and your points go back to 0; your best stays. Earning a point shows a +1 (from the next update it flies into the counter; the first point and a miss get a full-screen moment). Posts say "Answered @sam in 2h". The profile points card shows your points, your best, and soon the last mates you answered.

name: feed
purpose: The feed of friends' workouts: what's in it and how the cards work
summary:
Workouts from the people you follow, full screen, one at a time, newest first, plus only your own latest post in its place by time; older posts stay on your profile. Pull down to refresh; posts stay visible while another page loads.
• Feed rows remain fresh from the server, while valid photo links and native image caches are reused so the same post or avatar no longer visibly reloads on refresh.
• Cards show poster, time, points, caption and tags; pinch to zoom, like, comment or open a profile. Owners can edit a caption for one hour or delete their own post.
• A live countdown shows how long the feed remains open.

name: feed-lock
purpose: When the feed is open, when it locks, and what it says
summary:
Posting opens your feed for 24 hours. If you're tagged in that time, the feed locks when the 24 hours end. If you're not, it stays open until someone tags you, and then it locks until you post your answer.
• A new person starts locked. Miss a tag and it stays locked until a friend tags you again.
• While locked, friends' photos and captions are hidden on the server, not just on the phone. Your own posts always show.
• A locked feed says who tagged you and how long you've got, or that you can post again when a friend tags you. An open feed shows a live countdown (hours, minutes, seconds) to when it would lock, or, if you're tagged, "@sam tagged you · locks in" with the clock.

name: likes-and-comments
purpose: Likes, double tap to like, and the comments sheet
summary:
Tap the heart or double tap the photo to like (double tap only likes, never unlikes). Counts update live.
• Comments open in a full-height sheet titled "N comments", oldest first, and update live. Comments can't be edited or deleted yet.
• Each comment has a heart and a count; tap the count to see who liked it and open their profiles.
• Posts opened from a profile look exactly like the feed, with likes and comments.

name: profiles
purpose: Your profile, other people's profiles, and Settings
summary:
Profiles show photo, search, friends, Points, Best, suggestions and a paged workout grid. Remote avatars and workout images use native caching so returning to a profile is immediate.
• Settings is a page sheet: the appearance icon sits inline with the Settings title; Notifications opens the phone's controls; Security and privacy contains Blocked users, Log out and Delete account; Help sits under Support.
• Other profiles offer Follow, Message, Block and Report. Not built yet: edit profile or changing name/username after sign-up.

name: friends-and-suggestions
purpose: Following, who counts as a friend, and "Suggested for you"
summary:
Follow anyone. Friends are people who follow each other, and only friends can be tagged. The friends list shows names, never numbers.
• "Suggested for you" shows friends of friends, ranked by how many people you share. Someone new sees popular people instead. It skips people you already follow and anyone blocked either way.
• Coming: a profile shows when someone follows you, so you can follow back in one tap.

name: search-people
purpose: Finding people by name or username
summary: Tap the magnifier on your profile or in Messages, or "Find friends" on an empty feed, to get a frosted full-screen search. It matches part of a username, display name, first name or last name, and shows points. Blocked people are hidden. Tapping a result opens their profile, where you can follow or message them.

name: messages
purpose: Private chats and message requests
summary: Private chats like PingMee-v2: the first message is a request to accept, decline or block; edit for 15 minutes; unsend. Coming in the next update: hold a message for Apple's own menu with a quick emoji row (👍 ❤️ 😂 🔥 💪 👏) and a + for the full emoji keyboard, reaction badges under bubbles, double-tap to ❤️. Build 13 adds the emoji keyboard button with search and suggestions.

name: notifications
purpose: The bell and the notifications list
summary:
The bell lists likes, comments, follows, tags, answered tags, missed tags, points lost to a missed tag and friends who joined from your invite, with unread dots. Closing the list marks everything read; blocked people are filtered out.
• Each line uses the same words as the alert on the phone for the same thing. A tag reads "You've been tagged by @sam. 48 hours to post your Mahi!".
• Tapping the avatar opens their profile. Not built yet: tapping a post notice to open that post.

name: push-notifications
purpose: Alerts on the phone: built, waiting to be switched on
summary: Built and waiting for build 13 (owner, 2026-10-07: set up through EAS at the production build). Then every tag, answer, like, comment, message and missed tag sends a push; the first time, Mahi asks with its own page before the phone's question. The switch goes on for everyone at once, never for one account first. There are 38 old alerts queued that will be cleared before the first phone registers.

name: moderation-safety
purpose: Block, report and banned accounts
summary:
Block asks first, then removes follows both ways, hides each other's posts and profiles, cancels any open tag between you and freezes the chat. Unblocking restores the chat; you'd need to follow each other again.
• Report a person, a post, a comment or a message, with a reason. Staff review every report and can hide a post, remove a comment or message, warn, suspend or ban, always with a note that's logged. Hidden things disappear for everyone but staff and can be put back.
• You can see your own account standing. Being suspended or banned signs you out.
• Coming: an automatic check that flags worrying posts and comments for staff; it hides nothing by itself.

name: invites
purpose: Invite links and six-character codes for friends who aren't on Mahi yet
summary: Invite links open Mahi straight from Messages or WhatsApp when it is installed, and show a web page (who tagged you, 48 hours, Get Mahi) when it isn't. Invite a mate any time from the camera's waiting card; joining makes you follow each other, and a tag starts only if one came with the link. Your invites (Profile, Settings, and "See your invites" with a count on the camera) lists every link: waiting, joined (with who), expired or cancelled; resend once a day up to 3 times; cancel stops the link. Build 13 adds inviting straight from your contacts and an App Clip so the link works before Mahi is installed. Invites and opens are counted in PostHog.

name: navigation-and-design
purpose: Swipes, the glass bar, sheets, fonts, colours and the design values
summary:
Mahi opens on the camera. The screens sit in one row, left to right: messages, the feed, the camera, then your profile. Swipe sideways to move along the row, from any page including your profile; there is no up or down swiping. Pages snap into place with a light tap you can feel.
• On the newest App Store build, the phone's own tab bar sits along the bottom in the same order: tap a tab to jump there, and it follows your swipes. Older builds have a floating glass bar on the left of the camera instead, and the same glass bar along the bottom of the feed, profile and messages, so every page has a tap to every other; hold and drag along it to switch. Sheets slide up and swipe down to close; menus and date pickers are the iPhone's own; passwords and codes fill themselves in.
• Inter font throughout, all wording in sentence case. Calm off-white and off-black with a cyan accent for anything you can tap and gold for points, in light and dark mode. Every colour, size and spacing comes from one shared set of values, so the app and the website stay consistent.
• Apple's own icons are on for everyone on the newest App Store build.

name: server-and-numbers
purpose: Rules enforced on the server, time zones, and the figures only we can see
summary:
Who can post, the three tags, the 48 hours, the Mahi points and the feed lock are all enforced on the server, so an old or tampered app can't get round them. Posting is all or nothing, and a retry never makes a duplicate.
• Every post is dated in the poster's own local day, and quiet hours follow their clock.
• Our numbers, read only by us: tags sent, answered and missed with the typical answer time; posts and posters; invites sent and claimed; and how many accounts posted each week.

name: waitlist-website
purpose: The one-page waitlist site and its sign-up form
summary:
One page: what Mahi is, how it works in three steps (post when a friend tags you, every post tags three friends, every answer earns a Mahi point), and a form for name, email, how you train and whether you'd test early versions. Sign-ups land in a list with an email alert each.
• The site only rebuilds when we ask it to, by editing one file in the repo.

name: analytics-posthog
purpose: What we measure in PostHog and the feature switches
summary:
Counted: sign-ups and log-ins, password resets, posts, tags sent, answered and missed, points lost, invites shared and claimed, follows and unfollows, likes, comments, messages, feed unlocks, pushes opened, blocks and reports. Each action is counted once, only after the server has saved it.
• One person per account: a phone that opens Mahi signed out no longer counts as a new person.
• Founder metrics dashboard: active people per day, week and month, how often people come back (day 1, 7, 30 and weekly), new sign-ups, sign-up to first post to first answered tag, actions per week, and who has gone quiet. https://eu.posthog.com/project/130791/dashboard/1004897
• The database's own totals (the numbers of record) are copied into PostHog every day and shown on the dashboard.
• Posted here automatically: every new sign-up (and whether they came from an invite), the dashboard every Monday morning, an alert if a day passes with no one active, and an alert if a week passes with no sign-ups.
• Invites dashboard: links shared, invite pages opened, Mahi opened from a link, sign-ups that came with an invite, and (from the database) links made, joined and joined then posted, every week. Posted here every Monday. https://eu.posthog.com/project/130791/dashboard/1005256
• Every event says which app update sent it (for example 12.30), so numbers can be checked per update.
• Fifteen feature switches can turn a feature off from outside the app without an update, in case one misbehaves.
• Errors and crashes go to Sentry: see #error-reporting-sentry.

name: error-reporting-sentry
purpose: What goes wrong in the app, as Sentry sees it
summary:
Every failure a person could notice is sent to Sentry with a plain title saying where it broke and why, for example "posts.create failed: <reason> [code 42501]", plus the server's own explanation and the taps just before it. Passwords, codes, messages and emails are never sent.
• One problem shows as one issue however many people hit it. Wrong passwords, cancelled pickers and declined permissions are not counted as bugs.
• Test phones and App Store phones are kept apart, and each report says which update it came from.
• Crash lines point to the real code once each update's maps are uploaded (automatic for preview updates).
• Sentry: https://mahi-org.sentry.io (project react-native).

name: apple-ios-store
purpose: App Store builds, TestFlight, review notes and what Apple requires
summary: Nothing is in the App Store yet; updates go to our three registered test iPhones. Use this channel for App Store builds, review feedback and Apple's requirements (in-app delete account is already built for that).

name: android-play-store
purpose: Android builds and Play Store listing
summary: Android has never been built yet; the app and the site say "Coming to iPhone and Android". Use this channel for the first Android build, device testing and the Play Store listing.

name: ota-updates
purpose: Over-the-air updates: what went out, when, and how to check it on a phone
summary:
Most changes reach phones over the air without an App Store release. The Settings version line shows the build and update number. To check an update landed: force-quit and open the app twice.
• Latest production release: 12.16 — Maximus's Q1–Q10 answers, mixed friend/non-user tags, post deletion with permanent first-post history, faster cached media, and reorganised Settings.

name: maintenance
purpose: Bugs, crashes, server upkeep and anything that needs fixing
summary: Report anything broken here with the phone, the version line from Settings, and what you were doing. Server-side checks and database changes are recorded here too.

name: repo-structure
purpose: How the code and the project are organised
summary: One repository: the iPhone app, the website and the server rules together, with automated tests for all three (over 1,300 app checks and 300 database checks). The rules of the road for working in it live in the repo's own docs.

name: project-planning-strategy
purpose: Product decisions, priorities and what's next
summary: Decisions that shape the product live here. Decided so far: post only when tagged (never to show off), Mahi points (one per post that answers a tag, back to nought on a missed tag, best always visible; not a streak, and no daily streak for now), no rest days or calendars, and the 24-hour feed rule. Open: what happens to a flagged post, the invite website, push notifications setup, Android.

name: feature-flags
purpose: Every app switch, what it controls, and whether it's on, off or partly rolled out
summary:
Every switch the app reads and who has it. Change them in PostHog; a switch missing there counts as off.
• `auth-google-signin` — "Continue with Google" (not set up yet). *Off since 8 October, until it's set up.*
• `ios-sf-symbols` — Apple's own icons on iPhone. *On, 100% (6 October).*
• `camera-tap-focus` — Tap the camera to focus and set brightness there. *Off until the next App Store build.*
• `identity-verification` — Didit identity and age checks. *Off until the next App Store build and the Didit account are ready.*
• `purchases` — Subscriptions and in-app purchases through RevenueCat. *Off until the next App Store build and RevenueCat are ready.*
• `video-posts` — Each shot can be a photo or a video (up to 15 seconds), with sound on/off. *Off for everyone. Needs the next App Store build first.*
• `tag-slots` — One tag screen: slots that show where each tag is at, in-app invites, links sent on tap. *Off (not created). After a phone check.*
• `push-core` — The full-screen "turn on notifications" page and the camera's reminder line. *Off (not created). Goes on once the sending service is live and tested on one phone.*
Build 13 off switches, all *on, 100%* since 7 October:
• `contacts-finder` — Find your mates from contacts.
• `widget-tagger-photo` — The tagger's photo on the lock screen and widget.
• `widget-background-refresh` — The widget refreshing while Mahi is closed.
• `emoji-keyboard` — The emoji keyboard in messages.
• `message-reactions` — Hold a message to react, double tap for a heart.
• `point-fly-in` — The +1 flying into the counter.
• `feed-develop` — Locked posts clearing one by one after you post.
• `tag-drain-ring` — The ring around the tagger in the last 6 hours.
• `answered-stamp` — The "Answered @sam" stamp.
• `camera-tab-badge` — A number on the Camera tab while a tag waits.
• `miss-roll-down` — The counter rolling down after a miss.
• `profile-points-card` — The profile points card with your last three mates.
• `share-to-mahi` — Share a photo from Photos into Mahi.
• `shutter-sound` — Apple's shutter sound.
• `private-accounts` — Public/private accounts, Controls, follow requests. *Off until build 13 is on phones.*
Held back, not released yet — *off* since 8 October, and off in the app until switched on:
• `auth-apple-signin` — Sign in with Apple on the welcome screen.
• `live-activity` — A friend's tag on the lock screen, Dynamic Island and widget.
• `control-post-workout` — "Post a workout" in Control Centre.
• `spotlight` — Mahi in Spotlight search.
• `siri-shortcuts` — Mahi in Siri and Shortcuts.
Now standard, no switch (deleted from PostHog 7 October): welcome cards, password reset, delete account, the camera's small window, comment likes, "Invite 3 friends", invite links, open-tags banner, feed lock explainer, notifications, the glass bar, `context-menu-preview`, `content-reports`.
Last checked 8 October 2026.

name: apple-icons
purpose: Apple's own icon set on iPhone
summary: Mahi's icons switch to Apple's own symbols on iPhone, so they match the rest of the phone and scale with the text size people choose. Android keeps today's icons. Ships in the next App Store build and stays switched off until we turn it on.

name: hold-to-preview
purpose: Hold to pop a post or chat up for a quick look
summary: Hold a post, a profile square or a chat to pop it up with Apple's own menu for a quick look. Coming in the next update: hold a message for the emoji reaction row and menu, and hold to react on more places.

name: camera-features
purpose: Flash, tap to focus, better photos and stronger feedback
summary: Flash for your view and a bright-screen flash for selfies, sharper photos, steadier video and clearer vibrations are already live for everyone. Tap to focus and set brightness where you tap comes with the next App Store build and stays switched off until we turn it on.

name: identity-verification
purpose: Checking people are who they say they are (Didit)
summary: Lets Mahi confirm a person's identity or age with a quick ID and face check through Didit, for example before someone can post or message. The parts that need the App Store go into the next build and stay switched off; turning it on later is an update, once we decide where it applies and set up the Didit account.

name: subscriptions
purpose: Paid plans and in-app purchases (RevenueCat)
summary: Gets Mahi ready to sell subscriptions or one-off purchases through the App Store, managed with RevenueCat. The parts that need the App Store go into the next build and stay switched off; turning it on later is an update, once the plans, prices and RevenueCat account are set up.

name: haptics
purpose: How Mahi feels in the hand: every vibration and what it means
summary: Mahi gives a small, distinct vibration at the moments that matter: a crisp click on the shutter, a soft one when the camera flips, a confirmation when a post and its tags send, a stronger bump when you earn a Mahi point, a warning when your feed locks and a success when it opens again, a light tick for likes and switching screens, and a buzz when something fails. Every vibration goes through one shared set, so the same moment always feels the same everywhere.

name: questions-and-answers
purpose: Questions the team needs to answer before something is built or switched on
summary: Each question is its own message, with the choices to pick from. Answer in its thread; once it's decided it goes into the decisions list and the work goes ahead.

name: staff-portal
purpose: The staff website for reviewing reports and taking moderation actions
summary:
A private website for Mahi staff. Staff sign in with their Mahi account and land on an overview: new reports, reports being looked at, today's reports, who is suspended or banned, and the latest actions. Reports can be filtered and searched; each report shows what was reported, who reported it and the person's history. Actions sit in a Safe box (dismiss, show again, restore) and a Serious box (hide a post, remove a comment or message, warn, suspend, ban); each needs a note and a confirm step, and goes in the audit log. Admins alone can ban.
• Works on a computer today; putting it on its own web address is the next step. Counts and search cover the newest 200 reports.

name: openai-moderation-setup
purpose: Setting up the OpenAI key and automated content moderation
summary:
The automated check for concerning posts and comments, flagging them for staff review.
• Needs the OpenAI API key stored in Supabase Vault, the `moderate-content` function deployed, and the moderation secret in place.
• Once live, new reports trigger an automatic check. Staff still decide on any action. See docs/moderation.md for the full owner steps.

name: find-your-mates
purpose: Finding mates from your contacts, and who is on Mahi
summary: From build 13: Find your mates shows which of your contacts are already on Mahi (with a Follow button) and lets you invite the rest by text with a ready-made message. It appears once after sign-up, and from Settings, Your invites and the camera. Your contacts stay private: only scrambled codes of numbers and emails leave the phone, Mahi saves nothing, and matching is limited to 10 checks an hour. Not yet on phones; needs build 13.

name: lock-screen-and-widgets
purpose: The lock-screen countdown, Dynamic Island and the home-screen widget
summary: From build 13: while a mate's tag is open, the lock screen and Dynamic Island show "@sam is waiting on you" with a live countdown that turns yellow under 6 hours; tapping it opens the camera. A home-screen widget (small and medium) shows the same, or your points and best when nothing is waiting. The widget keeps the soonest tag on the phone so it can count down with Mahi closed (the one exception to the no-stored-data rule). The tagger's photo is being added. Not yet on phones; needs build 13.

name: build-13
purpose: Everything in the next App Store build and where it stands
summary: Build 13 (not built yet) carries: Find your mates from contacts; the lock-screen countdown and home-screen widget; the native emoji keyboard button in comments, messages and captions; push notifications switched on; Sign in with Apple; Share to Mahi from the Photos app; a Post a workout control for Control Centre; Spotlight search of your mates; Siri shortcuts; Apple's own shutter sound; background refresh for the widget; and an App Clip so an invite link works before Mahi is installed. The owner runs the build (EAS creates the Apple records). Phone checks are listed in docs/HANDOVER.md.

name: tips-and-guidance
purpose: One-time tips, reminders and the words that explain how Mahi works
summary: Six one-time tips appear where people get lost: your points, the two photos, tagging 3 mates, the locked feed, waiting for a tag, and a tag arriving. On iPhone they are Apple's own pop-up bubbles pointing at the exact button; older builds get a spotlight version. Each shows once per account per phone. Reminders: the tag clock turns yellow under 6 hours, a toast says how long is left when you open Mahi with a tag waiting, and the camera says who is waiting on you and what a miss would cost.
